findings.title: Verification walkthrough asks for baseline/isolation runs the branch cannot produce
findings.description: Step 3 lists four gate runs, two of which require counter-gating: "Baseline (S=1, counter-gating — should reproduce slice 145 ~38 TPS)" and "Cell subdivision only (S=3, counter-gating)". But Intervention 1 makes the `break` permanent (line 25, "Replace counter-gating"), with no flag to disable it. On this branch every S=1 and S=3 run has early exit enabled, so the 38 TPS counter-gating baseline and the "subdivision only" isolation point cannot be reproduced as written — yet A2 uses that baseline as its ≥5× denominator and Step 3 says "force_total ≥ 5× reduction vs baseline." The implementing task file resolves this by capturing the baseline from `main` (T1) and forbidding re-running counter-gating on the branch (T12). The walkthrough should be corrected to state that the baseline is a recorded value from `main` and that only the combined (S=3 + break) configuration is measurable here; otherwise the gate as documented cannot be executed.

findings.title: A7 seam is claimed "preserved" but is functionally bypassed by the new break
findings.description: Option A states the removed seam "becomes unreachable when the break fires, but remains the documented swap point for distance-ranked selection (still needed for slice design A7)." A count-based `break` at the top of the `for kk` loop is precisely the opposite of what a distance-ranked k-nearest kernel needs (it must keep evaluating candidates and compare distances, then exit on a distance threshold, not at `k_found >= k_max`). So the future A7 slice must now change two sites — the new break and the seam — rather than swapping one. This is a hidden coupling to a named future consumer: the seam is preserved in name only, and the doc's cross-slice claim (line 112) that it "remains intact" overstates it. The design should acknowledge that A7 must replace the break as well, or define the seam at a level (e.g., the whole per-agent scan policy) that genuinely remains the single swap point.

findings.title: Config surface for `S` is ambiguous and inconsistent with the implementing task
findings.description: Intervention 2 and the Component Interactions diagram define `S` as a `BenchConfig`/workload value ("Add ... to the bench configuration," "reads from config"), but the walkthrough expresses it only as an ad-hoc CLI override (`--subdivision-factor 3`, lines 165-175). No authoritative config surface is specified. The implementing task file instead creates a `mid-flock-50k-s3.yaml` workload variant with `subdivision_factor: 3` embedded (T11/T12). Relatedly, "No changes to ... Parity test infrastructure" (line 104) sits awkwardly with the task's T11b fixture change needed for S=3 parity testing. These are not blocking, but the design should name one canonical way S enters `BenchConfig` so the gate config is reproducible.
